long_biography.plain_text:
Buying Ligier brought Cyril Bourlon de Rouvre back to Formula 1 after his unsuccessful ownership of AGS. He retained Ligier’s established name and staff, then recruited Martin Brundle and Mark Blundell for the 1993 season. His choice reflected their experience and technical feedback, despite criticism of an English pairing at a French team.

De Rouvre also negotiated a supply of Williams semi-automatic gearboxes because Ligier’s own transmission would not be ready in time. The arrangement paired proven equipment with Renault engines as the team sought to recover its competitiveness. Ligier finished fifth in the constructors’ championship that season. His ownership ended with the team’s sale to Flavio Briatore in 1994.
